slides.text:
Programs read text from somewhere: the keyboard, a file, a network. `bufio.Scanner` cuts that text into pieces (lines, words, characters) and hands them over one by one.

A real program reads the keyboard like this:

Here the source is always a string, so every output is the same each time. Swapping it for the keyboard changes nothing else.

You will read lines, split input, handle errors and limits, and read values with `fmt.Sscan`.

A scanner wraps a source and moves through it one piece at a time. By default a piece is a line.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
scanner = wrap(source)
while scanner has a next line:
    line = current line
    use line

slides.text: `Scan` moves forward and says whether there was something to read. `Text` gives the current piece, without its newline. That is why the usual loop is `for scanner.Scan()`.

exercises.title: Read lines
exercises.guide: Read a text one line at a time with a scanner.

chunks.guide: The text to read. In a real program it would come from the keyboard or a file.
A scanner reads from a source. `strings.NewReader` turns a string into one.

notes.text: Cuts a source into pieces, one line at a time
Makes the string readable like a file

chunks.guide: `Scan` moves to the next line and says if there is one. `Text` returns it.

notes.text: Reads the next line. False when the input ends
The line just read, without its newline

output.text:
line: alpha
line: beta
line: gamma

exercises.title: Number the lines
exercises.guide: Print each line with its number, and see what counts as a line.

chunks.guide: A blank line sits between two words, and the text ends with a newline.
`%q` quotes each line so the empty one is visible. The last newline adds no line.

notes.text: Quotes the text, so an empty line shows as two quotes

exercises.title: Skip blank and comment lines
exercises.guide: Print only the lines that carry data.

chunks.guide: Some lines are comments, some are blank, and one has extra spaces.
chunks.text:
input := "# servers
web1

  web2  
# off
web3
"
    scanner := bufio.NewScanner(
        strings.NewReader(input),
    )

chunks.guide: Trim each line, skip blank ones and comments with `continue`, and print the rest.

notes.text: Jumps to the next line without printing this one

exercises.title: Print every line
exercises.guide: Create a scanner over the reader and print each line.

exercises.title: How many lines?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.code:
r := strings.NewReader("one\ntwo\n\n")
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(r)
n := 0
for scanner.Scan() {
    n++
}
fmt.Println(n)
exercises.explanation: The text holds `one`, `two` and an empty line: the final newline ends the empty line and adds nothing after it.

exercises.title: Sum the numbers
exercises.guide: Add up the numbers, one per line, ignoring lines that are not numbers.

chunks.guide: One line is not a number.
Convert each line to a number, and skip the ones that fail.
Print the sum of the valid lines.

slides.text:
How the input is cut is a choice. The default rule cuts lines, and `bufio` has two more: `ScanWords` and `ScanRunes`.

You pick one with `Split` before the first `Scan`.

exercises.title: Read word by word
exercises.guide: Change the scanner so each piece is a word, not a line.

chunks.guide: The words run across two lines and one gap has two spaces.
chunks.text:
input := "go is  fun\nand fast"
    scanner := bufio.NewScanner(
        strings.NewReader(input),
    )

chunks.guide: Choose how to cut the input. It goes before the first `Scan`.

notes.text: Sets the rule that cuts the input into pieces
Cuts on spaces and newlines, skipping empty gaps

chunks.guide: The loop is the same: only the pieces changed.

exercises.title: Read character by character
exercises.guide: Cut the input into single characters and measure each one.

chunks.guide: `ScanRunes` makes every character a piece.

notes.text: One piece per character, not per byte

chunks.guide: Print each character and its size in bytes.

exercises.title: Print the words
exercises.guide: Print the text word by word, not line by line.

exercises.title: How long is the line?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.code:
r := strings.NewReader("hi\r\nbye")
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(r)
scanner.Scan()
fmt.Println(len(scanner.Text()))
exercises.explanation: Line scanning drops the newline and also a carriage return before it, so a Windows line ending leaves just `hi`.

exercises.title: Parse key=value lines
exercises.guide: Split each line into a key and a value, and report the lines that do not fit.

chunks.guide: A small config text, with one broken line.
Cut each line at the equals sign. A line without one is reported and skipped.

output.text:
host -> db
port -> 5432
skip: bad line

exercises.title: Read a header, then the rows
exercises.guide: Read the first line on its own, then loop over the rest.

chunks.guide: The first line names the columns.
One call to `Scan` outside a loop reads exactly one line.

notes.text: Reads one line now. The loop below continues after it

chunks.guide: The loop starts at the second line, because the first was read.
Print the sum of the quantities.

slides.text: A scanner has a limit: a line longer than its buffer stops the loop. The loop ends the same way as at the end of the input, so only `Err` tells you something went wrong.

When the text has a known shape, `fmt.Sscan` and `fmt.Sscanf` read values straight into variables. They need the address of each variable, written with `&`: take it as a recipe for now, the pointers course explains it.

exercises.title: A line that is too long
exercises.guide: Set a size limit, read until a line breaks it, and check the error.

chunks.guide: The second line is longer than the limit we set next.
chunks.text:
input := "ok\nthis line is far too long\nnext"
    scanner := bufio.NewScanner(
        strings.NewReader(input),
    )

chunks.guide: Shrink the limit to 8 bytes, to see what happens past it.

notes.text: Sets the starting space and the biggest line allowed

chunks.guide: The loop stops at the long line, as if the input had ended.
After the loop, ask why it stopped.

notes.text: The failure that ended the loop, or nil at the normal end

output.text:
ok
error: bufio.Scanner: token too long

exercises.title: Why call Err?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick what the last check is for.
options: Counts how many lines were read
Rewinds the scanner to read again
Tells a read failure from the normal end
Skips the lines that could not be parsed
exercises.explanation: `Scan` returns false both at the end of the input and on a failure. `Err` tells them apart: it is nil at the end.

exercises.title: Read values from a string
exercises.guide: Pull a word and a number out of a line of text.

chunks.guide: Two variables to fill.
chunks.text:
var name string
    var age int

chunks.guide: `Sscan` splits the text on spaces and fills each variable in order.

notes.text: Reads values out of a string, separated by spaces
Lets Sscan fill name. Pointers come later

chunks.guide: `n` counts the values filled, and `err` is nil when all went well.

exercises.title: Read with a format
exercises.guide: Read two numbers from a pattern, then see how a bad input fails.

chunks.guide: Two numbers to fill.
A format describes the shape of the text, with the verbs you know from printing.

notes.text: Reads values from text that matches a format
Two numbers with a dash between them

chunks.text:
n, err := fmt.Sscanf("10-20", "%d-%d", &low, &high)
    fmt.Println(low, high, n, err)

chunks.guide: The second number is not a digit, so only one value is read.

exercises.title: Read a range
exercises.guide: Read the two ends of a range with a format, then print them and how many values were read.

exercises.title: Read with a reader
exercises.guide: Read lines with a reader, and keep the last line that has no newline.

chunks.guide: A reader gives more control than a scanner. The text has no final newline.

notes.text: Reads a source piece by piece, with no size limit

chunks.guide: Print what came back, then stop at the end. The last piece arrives together with the end-of-input error.

notes.text: Reads up to the delimiter, which stays in the result
The error that means the input has ended
